rules.title: Boundaries are explicit.
rules.text: Dependency runs one way — interface to application, application to domain. The domain knows nothing of the framework, the database or the transport. A boundary is crossed by a written decision.

rules.title: The smallest change that works.
rules.text: No abstraction for a future that has not arrived; whatever stops being used goes in the same change.

rules.title: Verify before claiming.
rules.text: Nothing is done because it compiles. It is done when the gates pass and it has been seen in the production build.

rules.title: Decisions are written down.
rules.text: What cannot be read off the code goes into a dated record with at least two options compared.

meta.title: Star Wars API — Case study — Bruno Galván
meta.description: A serverless API on AWS Lambda that translates SWAPI characters into Spanish and stores them in DynamoDB, in four layers.

headline: A serverless API.
In four layers.
starwars-api.summary: An API on AWS Lambda that translates SWAPI characters into Spanish and stores them in DynamoDB.
starwars-api.context: A project built with the Serverless Framework. It exposes two groups of REST endpoints: one reads from SWAPI and returns each character with its fields in Spanish; the other creates and queries characters in a DynamoDB table.

layers.name: Presentation
layers.text: Express routes and controllers, one per source: dynamo and swapi. Each controller maps a character to Spanish field names.

layers.name: Domain
layers.text: The IPeopleRepository interface and a CustomError with a factory per HTTP status.

layers.name: Infrastructure
layers.text: DynamoDBPeopleRepository implements the interface with the Scan, Get and Put commands of the AWS SDK v3.

layers.name: Data
layers.text: The DynamoDB client and the Person model.

decisions.title: One function
decisions.text: Serverless declares a single function with one HTTP event that catches every route; Express routes inside it through serverless-http.

decisions.title: Permissions for one table
decisions.text: The IAM role grants exactly five DynamoDB actions, and only on the ARN of the service’s table.

decisions.title: The table as code
decisions.text: The table is declared in the same serverless.yml, with a string partition key, id.

decisions.title: Required configuration
decisions.text: env-var marks the SWAPI URL, the region and the table name as required: without them the function does not start.

meta.title: IDBI Invoice Recorder — Case study — Bruno Galván
meta.description: A Laravel REST API that records XML invoices in the background, behind JWT, with single-action controllers, Form Requests and API Resources.

headline: XML invoices.
Recorded in the background.
idbi-invoice.summary: A Laravel REST API that records XML electronic invoices, extracts their data and queries them with filters, behind JWT.
idbi-invoice.context: A technical challenge for IDBI. The API takes one or more XML files, processes them on a queue and emails a summary of the invoices recorded and of those that failed.

layers.name: Versioned routes
layers.text: routes/api.php loads the public v1 routes and, inside a group with the jwt.verify middleware, the protected ones.

layers.name: Single-action controllers
layers.text: Each endpoint is a class with __invoke; the invoice ones list, record, delete, total and regularize.

layers.name: Form Requests and API Resources
layers.text: GetVouchersRequest validates the page, the size, the dates and optional filters; VoucherResource shapes the response and loads lines and user only when asked.

layers.name: Service
layers.text: VoucherService reads the XML with SimpleXML and XPath over the UBL cbc and cac nodes.

decisions.title: Answer before processing
decisions.text: Recording answers 202 and dispatches the ProcessVouchers job, which implements ShouldQueue.

decisions.title: A domain event
decisions.text: When it finishes, the job emits VouchersCreated; a listener sends the email with successes and failures.

decisions.title: JWT as the guard
decisions.text: With tymon/jwt-auth, the api guard uses the jwt driver, and jwt.verify is an alias of Laravel’s Authenticate middleware.

decisions.title: A reproducible environment
decisions.text: compose.yml starts PHP 8.1 with Nginx, MySQL 8.0 and MailHog to read the emails.

meta.title: RIMAC Frontend — Case study — Bruno Galván
meta.description: A three-screen flow in React and TypeScript, with a Sass module per component, Axios and no state library.

headline: Three screens.
No state library.
rimac-frontend.summary: A three-screen flow in React and TypeScript: a form, the plans filtered by age, and a summary.
rimac-frontend.context: A technical test organised by Softtek. The app consumes a user API and a plans API, and is published on Netlify.

layers.name: Routes
layers.text: Three React Router routes: home, plans and summary.

layers.name: Styles
layers.text: One Sass module per component, following BEM.

layers.name: Data
layers.text: Axios in services/api, services that filter the plans by age, and hooks that hand them to the pages.

layers.name: State
layers.text: React local state and custom hooks: useUser and usePlans.

decisions.title: Four dependencies
decisions.text: react, react-dom, react-router-dom and axios. Nothing else at runtime.

decisions.title: Layers in the client
decisions.text: The API, the services, the hooks and the pages, each in its own folder.

decisions.title: Validated forms
decisions.text: The start form validates the document, phone and consents with validateForm, and continues only when they are valid.
